bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5761604792877056 Project: opensc Fuzzing Engine: libFuzzer Fuzz Target: fuzz_pkcs15_decode Job Type: libfuzzer_asan_opensc Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Heap-double-free Crash Address: 0x6020000005b0 Crash State: sc_pkcs15_free_object_content sc_pkcs15_free_object fuzz_pkcs15_decode.c Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Recommended Security Severity: High Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=libfuzzer_asan_opensc&range=201911110309:201911120312 Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=5761604792877056 Issue filed automatically.
bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 18890: In OpenSC's PKCS#15 public key decoder (sc_pkcs15_decode_pukdf_entry), when sc_asn1_decode partially decodes the attacker-controlled input and returns an error, the error handler calls free(der->value) on the allocated obj->content.value buffer without nulling the pointer. The caller's cleanup then frees the same pointer again via sc_pkcs15_free_object_content, producing a heap double-free.

source.description: sc_asn1_decode consumes the attacker-controlled PoC buffer; during partial decoding, asn1_decode_entry allocates a heap buffer and stores it in obj->content.value (via the der alias). The call returns a negative error code because the PoC is a malformed PKCS#15 public key entry.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled PoC bytes passed through the fuzzer harness into sc_pkcs15_decode_pukdf_entry as *buf/*buflen; the ASN1 decoder internally allocates a buffer from the decoded content and writes it into der->value (= obj->content.value) via the binding set at line 277.

sink.description: Second free of obj->content.value through the caller's cleanup path: sc_pkcs15_free_object calls sc_pkcs15_free_object_content, whose guard (obj->content.value && obj->content.len) passes because the dangling pointer is non-NULL and the stale decoded length is non-zero.

root_cause.description: On sc_asn1_decode error (r < 0), the error handler calls free(der->value) which frees obj->content.value, but does not null the pointer or zero obj->content.len. The dangling pointer persists in obj->content, enabling the caller's cleanup to free it a second time. The fix (commit 5557f34) removes this premature free entirely.

tainted_value_origin.description: The ASN1 decoder allocates a heap buffer from the attacker-controlled PoC bytes and stores its address in der->value (= obj->content.value). This pointer becomes the double-free target.

parser_admitted.description: The PoC's ASN1 structure is valid enough that sc_asn1_decode partially decodes it and allocates der->value before returning an error.

coarse_trace.summary: ASN1 decoding of attacker-controlled PoC buffer partially succeeds, allocating obj->content.value via asn1_decode_entry, then returns a negative error code.
Error handler frees obj->content.value (via der alias) without nulling the pointer or zeroing the length, creating a dangling pointer in the caller-owned obj struct.
Caller's cleanup via sc_pkcs15_free_object reaches sc_pkcs15_free_object_content, which frees the dangling obj->content.value a second time, triggering the ASan double-free.

fine_trace.note: Consumes the attacker-controlled PoC buffer through ASN1 public key decoding. The ASN1 entry binding at line 277 (sc_format_asn1_entry(asn1_rsakey_value_choice + 1, &der->value, &der->len, 0)) directs the decoder to store the 'direct' RSA key value into der->value, which aliases obj->content.value (der = &obj->content at line 220). asn1_decode_entry at asn1.c:1504 mallocs a 2-byte buffer and stores its address in obj->content.value. The overall decode then returns a negative error code because the PoC is malformed.

Error handler (guarded by r < 0) frees the heap buffer at obj->content.value. Neither der->value nor der->len is set to NULL/0 after the free. obj->content.value becomes a dangling pointer with obj->content.len still holding the stale non-zero decoded length. The patch (commit 5557f34) removes this free entirely, leaving the cleanup to the caller's sc_pkcs15_free_object_content.

After sc_pkcs15_decode_pukdf_entry returns error, the fuzzer calls sc_pkcs15_free_object(obj) (fuzz_pkcs15_decode.c:61) which calls sc_pkcs15_free_object_content(obj) (pkcs15.c:1912). The guard at line 2528 (obj->content.value && obj->content.len) passes because the dangling pointer is non-NULL and the stale decoded length is non-zero. Since obj->type is 0 (never assigned on the error path), the else branch at line 2536 calls free(obj->content.value), freeing the already-freed 2-byte heap region at 0x6020000005b0 a second time.

format.name: PKCS#15 ASN1-encoded public key entry
format.contract: A 24-byte ASN1/DER blob encoding a PKCS#15 public key entry that is structurally valid enough for sc_asn1_decode to partially decode and allocate the 'direct' RSA key value into obj->content.value, while being malformed enough to cause the overall decode to return a negative error code, triggering the premature free(der->value) error handler.
